research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding PNR as a sequence context
play-type labels derived from NBA play-by-play
derived possession records (initiator, play type, points) in the graph database
methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR change the PNR possession's PPP, compared with PNR possessions without that preceding DRIVE?
Are the DRIVE and PNR labels reliable enough to define the sequence and the outcome?
Do outcome-derived labels (points used to build the possession records) and foul endings make the PPP comparison circular or biased?
Which confounders (lineup, shot quality, defense, fouls, time in game) must be controlled before attributing any PPP difference to the sequence?

historical_evidence.finding: Backfilled play-type labels (921,514 possessions) failed verification against league bands and team identities: PNR share 28.7% vs band 20-28% (FAIL), PULL_UP 7.9% (FAIL), 2024-25 PULL_UP about 0-1% for many teams, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated, 3100 games with team PNR >33% (FAIL). PNR PPP 0.948 was recorded as PASS. Final verdict: FAIL.

Play-type labeling audit found OTHER possessions with 36% ending in fouls, which inflates OTHER PPP; DRIVE sits 12 points below the foul benchmark; PNR shows a 22% foul rate; initiation_type maps only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a play type. Verdict: artifact_found.

Scheme labels inferred backwards from opponent play-type PPP (523 within-game cells, 440 game pairs) gave near-uniform transition matrices, consistent with label noise. The record notes that outcome-inferred labels cannot separate a defensive change from the offense executing differently. No error rate was recorded for directly observed labels.

On one game (0042500101), matchup and play-by-play fields gave confident on-ball coverage labels for only 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60) of possessions. The switches_on field was not populated. Verdict: failed_gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using backfilled play-type labels from play-by-play as the basis for play-type analyses (PNR and PULL_UP most directly)
failed_approaches.why: Failed league-band and team-identity checks; 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy-calibrated; 2024-25 PULL_UP near 0% for many teams. The record does not quantify how much these failures bias any estimate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing PPP across play types (OTHER and DRIVE in particular) with the initiation_type mapping as the play-type source
failed_approaches.why: Foul endings inflate OTHER PPP (36% foul endings); DRIVE is 12 points below the foul benchmark; initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions. The record does not measure bias in downstream estimates.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Deriving observed on-ball coverage labels from the NBA matchup and play-by-play feeds
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates of 14.9% and 3.3% on one game; switches_on not populated; small sample (n=67/60).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme labels from outcome (opponent play-type PPP)
failed_approaches.why: Outcome-inferred labels cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution; near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

evidence_establishes: The project's play-type labels from play-by-play have failed validation: league-band and team-identity checks failed for PNR and PULL_UP (FAM:SF-APPA-030).
Foul endings contaminate PPP comparisons across play types, and the DRIVE label sits well below the foul benchmark (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Direct labels for on-ball coverage were rarely obtainable from these feeds in the one game examined (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Outcome-inferred labels are not a valid basis for testing defensive or offensive sequence effects (FAM:SF-APPA-005).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the DRIVE-to-PNR sequence effect on PNR PPP is real or null, since no retrieved record tests this sequence.
The size of label bias in the DRIVE or PNR categories on the specific sequence subset.
The number of DRIVE-then-PNR sequences in the data, or the power to detect an effect.
Whether the 82.8% proxy-calibrated PNR labels also affect the sequence (preceding-action) field.
Any result from tracking data or from more than one game for sequence labels.
own_inferences: The question is testable in principle only if the DRIVE and PNR labels are validated against an independent source (for example, a hand-coded sample of sequences) before any PPP comparison.
Because the PNR PPP is computed from the same points that define the derived possession records, a PPP comparison on labels partly built from outcomes risks circularity.
Teammate DRIVE-to-PNR sequences are a subset of PNR possessions, so exposure may be sparse at team-game level; the count must be checked before any power claim.
Lineup, shot quality, defensive matchup, and foul-ending differences could all move PNR PPP with or without the preceding DRIVE, so a raw comparison would be confounded.
uncertainties: The records do not say what share of the DRIVE-to-PNR sequence subset carries proxy-calibrated labels.
The records do not give an error rate for directly observed DRIVE or PNR labels.
Data version: the 2025-26 playoff file is partial before 2026-06-21, and the regular-season file is partial before 2026-04-13; the sample depends on which version is used.
No follow-up tool was called to check sequence counts or label coverage for DRIVE-to-PNR pairs; those facts are unknown here.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records show that play-type labels from these feeds failed validation (FAM:SF-APPA-030), that PPP comparisons across play types are contaminated by foul endings (FAM:SF-CHT-025), and that outcome-inferred or sparsely labeled categories are not testable (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPS-058). Given these, a direct test of the DRIVE-to-PNR PPP effect on the current labels would be built on unvalidated and outcome-contaminated inputs. The decision therefore moves from a proceed-as-posed plan to do_not_proceed until labels are validated.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR labels are 82.8% proxy-calibrated and the backfilled labels failed league-band and team-identity checks (FAM:SF-APPA-030); DRIVE is 12 points below the foul benchmark (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
The derived possession records use points as part of their construction, so a PNR PPP comparison on those records may be partly circular with the labels.
Lineup, shot quality, defensive matchup and foul endings can move PNR PPP independently of any preceding DRIVE; the question as posed has no control for these.
The count of teammate DRIVE-then-PNR sequences is not recorded in the retrieved evidence; if sparse, the test has little power (own inference).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the teammate DRIVE-to-PNR sequence effect on PNR PPP. The cited records concern label validity (play-type backfill, foul leakage in PPP, outcome-inferred scheme labels, on-ball coverage labels). They bear on whether the sequence can be measured reliably, not on whether the effect exists.

risks.text: Backfilled PNR and PULL_UP labels failed validation; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated (FAM:SF-APPA-030).

Foul endings (22% of PNR, 36% of OTHER) distort PPP, and the base rate of points per possession may differ between sequence and non-sequence PNRs (FAM:SF-CHT-025; own inference on the sequence subset).
Possession records carry points, so the sequence label and the PPP outcome share a source, creating circularity risk.
If the sequence label is assigned using information from after the PNR begins (for example, a play later coded as a DRIVE), the preceding-action condition may leak the outcome; own inference.
Lineup, defensive matchup, shot quality and fouls can affect PNR PPP without any DRIVE; a raw comparison is confounded.
The DRIVE-then-PNR subset size is unknown; a small subset gives little power to detect a modest PPP difference (own inference).
No reliability estimate for DRIVE or PNR labels is recorded; the test-retest or inter-coder reliability of the play-type labels is unknown.
If the test is run across many teammate-action pairs or play types, the number of comparisons must be controlled (own inference).
The data span 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the 2025-26 files are partial before their completion dates; labeling practice may differ across seasons (own inference).

design.estimand: Minimum viable test: the difference in PNR PPP between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE and PNR possessions not preceded by one, after label validation and adjustment for confounders. Not to be run until the preconditions below are met.
design.unit: Ball-handler PNR possession (one row per PNR possession), with the preceding teammate action identified from the ordered play-by-play.
design.sample: Only after label validation: a hand-coded sample of PNR and DRIVE labels, checked against play-by-play action types, from the regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 (complete files). Exclude partial 2025-26 files. Report the number of DRIVE-then-PNR sequences before any power claim; if too few, stop.
design.power: Not computed; to be set from the observed count of DRIVE-then-PNR sequences and a pre-specified minimum detectable PPP difference. Do not claim power without that count.
design.controls: Adjust for lineup and player fixed effects, defensive matchup, shot distance and result (excluded from the outcome if derived from points), game clock and score state, and foul endings (analyse with and without foul-ending possessions). Use only pre-PNR information for the sequence label to avoid lookahead.
design.falsification: A placebo sequence (a teammate SPOT-UP or other non-DRIVE action preceding PNR) should show no PPP difference; a PNR preceded by a non-teammate action should show none either. A material difference on the placebo would indicate label or confounding artifact.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary contrast (DRIVE-then-PNR vs. no DRIVE); any other play-type pairs are exploratory and corrected for multiple comparisons.
design.decision_rule: Conclude the effect is supported only if the adjusted PPP difference is positive, its interval excludes zero, the placebo sequences show no difference, and label-validation agreement meets a threshold fixed before analysis. Otherwise report uncertain or artifact; do not report a rejection without adequate power.
design.data_version: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (complete). 2025-26 regular season excluded until complete (from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (from 2026-06-21). Label version and backfill status must be recorded and fixed before analysis.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
